questions.title: What do you do if you hit the wrong ball and can’t find your real ball?
questions.question: You’ve played the wrong ball. Now you can’t find your own ball. What should you do next?

choices.text: Drop a new ball within one club-length of where you last hit your real ball and add one penalty shot.
Drop a new ball anywhere you like on the course and add two penalty shots.
Go back to the tee and start over with no penalty.
Keep playing with any ball you find.

questions.explanation: If you play the wrong ball and can’t find your real one, you must drop a new ball close to where you made your last proper shot—one club-length from that spot. You have to add one penalty shot to your score.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: An extra shot added to your score as a punishment when you break a rule.
The length of one of your golf clubs, used to measure how far you can drop your ball from a spot.

questions.teachingTip: Show kids how to measure one club-length on the grass, and where to drop a ball after losing their real one.
likelyMisconceptions: Some golfers might think you can just keep playing with any ball you find, but you can’t.
Some may think you can drop the ball anywhere, but it must be close to where you last hit your real ball.

questions.title: What to do if you can't find your original ball after hitting a wrong ball
questions.question: You have played a wrong ball and cannot find your original ball. What should you do according to the rules?

choices.text: Drop a ball within one club-length of where you last played your correct ball and add one penalty stroke
Drop a ball anywhere on the course and add two penalty strokes
Go back to the tee and start again with no penalty
Continue playing with any ball you find

questions.explanation: If the correct ball cannot be found after playing a wrong ball, you must return to where your last proper shot was made, drop a ball within one club-length of that spot, and add one penalty stroke (for a lost ball).
